connections.why: Understanding the purpose of business underpins how firms are classified
Sector and ownership choices shape the legal form a business takes
Growth ambitions often drive a change of legal structure
Ownership form determines whose objectives the business serves
Stakeholder aims include a motivated, productive workforce
Leadership style and structure directly affect employee motivation
Structure defines the roles a business recruits and trains for
Effective communication is essential to managing the workforce
Identifying customer needs requires market research to inform decisions
Research findings shape the product, price, place and promotion decisions
Strategy combines the mix elements to influence consumer decisions
Production method choices feed directly into a firm's cost structure
Quality systems carry costs that must be weighed against their benefits
Operational requirements and quality standards influence location decisions
Sources of finance are used to manage cash flow and working capital
Cash management connects to, but differs from, the profit shown in accounts
Retained profit links the income statement to the statement of financial position
Account statements provide the data for profitability and liquidity ratios
Cost and break-even analysis informs how much finance a business needs
Entering foreign markets depends on globalisation and exchange rates
Stakeholder pressure drives environmental and ethical decision-making
Interest-rate and tax changes affect the cost and choice of finance
Globalisation widens the choice of countries in which to locate operations
